stem: Three years after a cholecystectomy for gallstones, a 44-year-old woman digests fatty meals without difficulty. In this patient, bile is produced by which of the following structures?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None; the liver makes bile regardless of the gallbladder.
options.explanation: The digestive role of the liver is to produce bile and export it to the duodenum; bile emulsifies lipids, and its production is unaffected by gallbladder removal.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The storage organ is being cast as the producer, and it is absent here.
options.explanation: The gallbladder primarily stores, concentrates, and releases bile made by the liver; it does not synthesize bile, and this patient no longer has one.

options.label: C
options.misconception: A digestive gland is being credited with a hepatic product.
options.explanation: Pancreatic acini secrete enzyme-rich juice in response to CCK; bile is an alkaline, lipid-emulsifying solution produced by the liver.

options.label: D
options.misconception: The hormone-secreting mucosa is being cast as the bile source.
options.explanation: The duodenal mucosa secretes hormones such as secretin, CCK, and motilin that regulate digestion; bile itself arrives from the liver.

options.label: E
options.text: Duct cells of the common bile duct
options.misconception: The conduit is being cast as the source.
options.explanation: The bile duct is a passive conduit carrying bile from liver to duodenum; its lining cells do not synthesize bile.

context: Learning objective: separate bile production from bile storage. Hepatocytes produce bile — an alkaline solution that emulsifies lipids — and export it to the duodenum; the gallbladder only stores and concentrates it. Fat digestion therefore persists after cholecystectomy.
imageCaption: Bilirubin: spleen Hb breakdown -> unconjugated (albumin) -> hepatic conjugation -> bile -> gut bacteria -> urobilinogen/stercobilin; some urobilinogen -> urine.
